2. Official self-hosted Bitwarden — https://bitwarden.com/help/hosting-faqs/

Choose that deployment model if eliminating service dependencies is essential, and distinguish an external licensing or update contact from sending your vault authentication hash to an external vault service.

Vaultwarden supplies a self-hosted Bitwarden-compatible server and recommends Docker/Podman deployment with persistent storage. Configure each client to use your own server before creating or logging into the account. This is useful evidence for keeping server authentication under your control, rather than proof about every possible client cache or optional integration. Use HTTPS and keep both server and clients current: Bitwarden expressly does not guarantee compatibility with unofficial servers.

source_quote: This is the closest structural match in the evidence I examined. claim: PostgreSQL 9.5 release notes establish the underlying SQL features on January 7, 2016.
source_quote:
This is my strongest starting point if the application already uses PostgreSQL. A unique key prevents two producer attempts from registering the same logical task; workers claim different pending rows transactionally. For hour-long tasks, my proposed design uses a short claim transaction followed by a renewable lease, rather than holding a database transaction open throughout the computation. Completion must verify current ownership. Database results can be committed with the completion record; external operations need their own idempotency contract. Verify model/tensor placement and peak dedicated GPU memory during representative prompt processing as well as generation. CPU activity for tokenization or serving is distinct from spilling model inference to CPU. [Official build documentation](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/build.md).
